title: A dimension-free weak-type (1,1) bound for the Gaussian Riesz transforms
abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main results of Gutiérrez and Manfredi, "A direct obstacle proof of a dimension-free weak-type (1,1) bound for the Gaussian Riesz transforms" (arXiv:2610.26478). For the Gaussian measure dγₙ = π^{-n/2} e^{-|x|²} dx on ℝⁿ, the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck operator L = -½Δ + x·∇ and the normalized gradient D = 2^{-1/2}∇, the vector Riesz transform R_γ = D L^{-1/2} Π₀ has exactly one linear extension to L¹(γₙ) satisfying t·γₙ{|R_γ f| > t} ≤ 2‖f‖₁ for all t > 0, in every dimension n (Theorem 5.1). The proof goes through a Gaussian obstacle decomposition F = g + L^{1/2}u, with existence, uniqueness and the variational characterization of u, and the identification Dom(L^{1/2}) ⊆ W^{1,2}(γₙ) (Theorem 3.1). Also formalized: the principal-value realization of the extension by the Gaussian Riesz kernels (Proposition 5.3), the coordinatewise, historically normalized and unnormalized-measure bounds (Corollary 5.4), and the complex-valued bound with constant 8/π (Corollary 5.5). The Hermite basis of L²(γₙ) and the spectral calculus of L are built from Mathlib; there is no sorry and no axiom beyond propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
